title: NOAA GFS analysis, virtual Icechunk with a GRIB codec
description:
The same GFS analysis as a *virtual* Icechunk repository, with 272 variables. Its chunks are byte references into NOAA GRIB2 messages, and they decode with a `gribberish` codec.

This is the only codec case in the testbed, and it is the clearest argument for a codec profile. `gribberish` has implementations in Python and Rust and none in JavaScript. The repository opens, every metadata document parses, the grid is regular, and the chunk shape is [1, 721, 1440] for an amplification factor of 1. Every guard passes. Then every chunk read fails.

A virtual store inherits the compression of the files it references. A publisher who virtualizes GRIB inherits a codec no browser holds. That is why the codec check must read the codec chain from metadata and refuse up front, rather than let a tile load fail.

272 variables also exercises a client's layer cap.

Measured browser outcome, 2026-11-06: refused with "Virtual Icechunk repository (HTTPS) is compressed with gribberish. The browser cannot decode that." The guard read the codec chain from the array metadata and named the codec. The case transferred 0.48 MB in total and fetched no chunk.
